notes: Music no longer stops while you text. Every messaging app takes the audio for a moment to play its own short sound, and the app used to obey that exactly as it obeyed a phone call - so a one-second blip parked the song and nothing brought it back.

The app asks the phone one question before it obeys any interruption now: is a call really up? That is a fact Android publishes while a call is active or ringing, so a message tone, a notification sound or a voice note is no longer counted as a call.

A pause the system applies on its own is undone at any point in the song, not only in the opening seconds, and it works while the app is in the background. Only a pause you asked for, a song that ended or a real call is believed.

A real call still owns the speakers: a cellular or internet call pauses the song, the app stands down for it, and the song comes back where it was once the call is over. Nothing here fights a call for the audio.

The phone is only asked while it matters - a song on the deck, or a pause the app is already standing down for - and the asking stops the moment there is nothing left to protect, so no battery is spent on it for nothing.

A song that then plays untouched for a minute earns its protection back. Three refused stops in a row was the limit that kept the app from fighting a platform pause for ever, and it now resets after a quiet stretch instead of lasting the whole song.
